balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
TKO reports four segments: UFC and WWE (the two live-sports promotions, run separately since the September 2023 merger that created TKO), IMG (media, events and licensing, including the Endeavor businesses contributed at the same time) and Corporate & Other. Intersegment eliminations are negative and reconcile the four to consolidated Revenue.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: WWE and UFC have grown at different rates off different bases since the merger -- WWE's media-rights deals (Netflix, ESPN) have pushed its segment revenue past UFC's in recent periods, which the blended Revenue line hides entirely.

What to watch:

  • WWE vs UFC growth divergence quarter to quarter
  • IMG's event-calendar seasonality (concentrated around marquee properties)
  • Eliminations growing in step with segment revenue, not independently

segmentEbitda.title: Segment Adjusted EBITDA
segmentEbitda.content:
Each segment's Adjusted EBITDA as disclosed in the filings (excludes stock comp, transaction and integration costs, and other items TKO adds back). Corporate & Other is unallocated public-company overhead and merger-related costs, not a business line, so it runs persistently negative.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: UFC has historically carried a structurally higher margin than WWE (fewer, larger live events; a leaner cost base), so a rising WWE share of revenue does not translate one-for-one into consolidated margin -- read this beside the revenue split above.

What to watch:

  • WWE's margin converging toward or diverging from UFC's
  • IMG swinging between small positive and negative quarters
  • Corporate & Other's drag shrinking as one-off merger/integration costs roll off

revenueBySource.title: Revenue by source
revenueBySource.content:
Revenue split by stream rather than by segment: media rights (TV/streaming licensing, the largest and most contracted stream), live events & hospitality (ticketing, venue, travel packages), partnerships & marketing (sponsorships) and consumer products (merchandise, licensing).

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: media rights is the stream that re-rates in step changes at contract renewal (UFC's ESPN deal, WWE's Netflix and ESPN deals) rather than growing smoothly, so a flat or dipping quarter here is not the same signal as softness in the more cyclical live-events line.

What to watch:

  • Step changes at known renewal dates versus organic growth elsewhere
  • Live events & hospitality as the most seasonal, event-calendar-dependent line
  • Consumer products' small but growing share

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For TKO Group Holdings, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
